deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1953 preparatory material for what Grothendieck published as 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace' (Séminaire Bourbaki, exposé 113, 1955). On the previous page a 'fonction de Pólya' P on L^∞(K) (K a measure space of total mass |K|) is a functional that is (P1) invariant under equimeasurable rearrangement, (P2) convex and (P3') σ(L^∞,L^1)-lower semicontinuous. The epigraph A_P ⊂ R × L^∞ is then convex and weak*-closed. By Hahn–Banach, P is the supremum of its continuous affine minorants: P(f) = sup_i (a_i + L_i(f)) with L_i ∈ L^1.

Because of invariance, one may replace L_i(g) by its supremum over all g equimeasurable with f. That supremum is ∫ φ_{L_i} φ_f, where φ_h denotes the decreasing rearrangement on ]0,|K|] (the Hardy–Littlewood rearrangement inequality, 'prop. 2'). Writing φ_i = φ_{L_i} gives
(1) P(f) = sup_i (a_i + ∫_0^{|K|} φ_i φ_f), with φ_i decreasing on ]0,|K|].

This page then records the following.
(a) Converse: any functional defined on L^∞(K) by a formula (1) is a Pólya function.
(b) Additional condition 'P est croissante' (monotone). Grothendieck states this is equivalent to being able to take the φ_i positive.
(c) When the φ_i are positive, extend them by 0 on [|K|,+∞[ so they remain decreasing on R^+. This gives the K-independent formula
(2) P(f) = sup_i (a_i + ∫_0^∞ φ_i φ_f),
that is (3) P(f) = P*(φ_f), where
(4) P*(φ) = sup_i (a_i + ∫_0^∞ φ_i φ) is a Pólya function on R^+_*.
The point is that every monotone rearrangement-invariant convex lsc functional on any measure space factors through the decreasing rearrangement and a single functional on the half-line.

The long diagonal strokes cross out most of the body. A rotated marginal replacement states it more cleanly as 'Proposition 3': let P be a Pólya functional on ]0,ω[ (0<ω<∞); then P is of the form (1) with φ_i decreasing in L^1(]0,ω[). Below it is a heading 'Définition de φ_f' (the decreasing rearrangement).

The next page uses this. Prop. 4 states: if f, g are decreasing and ∫_0^t f ≤ ∫_0^t g for all t, then P(f) ≤ P(g) for every increasing Weyl/Pólya function. This is weak majorization ⇔ inequality for all monotone convex symmetric functionals. The proof is by Abel/integration by parts against decreasing positive φ.

Purpose: the classical Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya / Weyl majorization theory transposed to function spaces, and later to von Neumann algebras with a trace.
errors: The positivity issue is only sketched. The φ_i can be taken positive iff P is increasing. This needs an argument that a monotone convex weak*-lsc functional is a sup of positive affine minorants. It is true but not proved here.
Extending φ_i by 0 beyond |K| preserves monotonicity only if φ_i ≥ 0; Grothendieck implicitly notes this by adding '{+positives+}'. Without monotonicity of P, formula (2) on R^+ is not available.
For |K| = ∞, φ_f for f ∈ L^∞ may not be well-defined or finite in the usual way (e.g. constants). The marginal restatement restricts to ω < ∞, which avoids this gap.
Most of the body is struck through, so the definitive statement is the marginal Prop. 3.

ideas.what: Rearrangement-invariant convex weak*-lsc functionals on L^∞(K) are suprema of affine functionals a_i + ∫ φ_i φ_f, with φ_i decreasing and φ_f the decreasing rearrangement.
ideas.modern_name: Dual representation of rearrangement-invariant (symmetric) convex functionals; Lorentz/Luxemburg-type representation; Ryff/Calderón majorization duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya (finite case, 1929–34); G.G. Lorentz (1950s); W.A.J. Luxemburg (1955); Calderón (1966); Ryff (1965)
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace'

ideas.what: A monotone Pólya function on any measure space factors as P(f) = P*(φ_f), with P* a Pólya functional on the half-line R^+.
ideas.modern_name: Rearrangement-invariant functionals determined by their Luxemburg representation on (0,∞)

ideas.what: P is increasing iff the φ_i can be chosen positive.
ideas.modern_name: Monotone convex functions as sups of positive affine minorants

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material Grothendieck published in his 1955 Bourbaki exposé on rearrangements and convexity inequalities. The results are close to Lorentz, Luxemburg and Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya majorization theory, so nothing on the page appears absent from the record.
transcription_corrections: Most of the main body is crossed out by long diagonal strokes, not just the bracketed parts; the operative statement is the rotated marginal 'Proposition 3'.
'(soit boule [?] de K)' is more plausibly '(|K| = mesure totale de K)' or similar, explaining the interval ]0,|K|].
'... [?] P satisfait : ) P est croissante' is likely 'Inversement, ... si P satisfait : P_4) P est croissante', i.e. an additional axiom numbered like P_1–P_3.
The marginal 'Définition de φ_f' introduces φ_f as the decreasing function on ]0,|K|] equimeasurable with f (decreasing rearrangement).
